[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Introduction to Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) in PyTorch"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) is a foundational training technique in PyTorch designed for scaling large deep learning models across multiple GPUs. Unlike traditional Distributed Data Parallel (DDP), which replicates the entire model across every GPU, FSDP shards model parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across data-parallel ranks."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Why Use FSDP?"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Memory Efficiency: By sharding optimizer states, gradients, and parameters, FSDP drastically reduces the per-GPU memory footprint."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scalability: Enables the training of models with tens or hundreds of billions of parameters that would otherwise trigger Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Flexibility: Supports mixed precision, activation checkpointing, and advanced wrapping strategies."},{"order":7,"type":"heading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before implementing FSDP, ensure you have a compatible version of PyTorch installed along with a configured distributed environment using torch.distributed."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"import os
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from torch.distributed.fsdp import FullyShardedDataParallel as FSDP

def setup_distributed():
    dist.init_process_group("nccl")
    torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))"},{"order":10,"type":"heading","text":"Implementing FSDP in a Training Script"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"To apply FSDP to your model, you need to wrap your PyTorch nn.Module. It is a best practice to wrap specific transformer layers or sub-modules rather than just the root module to allow efficient communication overlap."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"from torch.distributed.fsdp.wrap import size_based_auto_wrap_policy
import functools

# Define a wrapping policy based on parameter size
my_auto_wrap_policy = functools.partial(
    size_based_auto_wrap_policy, min_num_params=1e8
)

# Initialize model and move to local GPU
model = MyLargeTransformerModel().cuda()

# Wrap with FSDP
model = FSDP(
    model,
    auto_wrap_policy=my_auto_wrap_policy,
    device_id=torch.cuda.current_device()
)"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Mixed Precision"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mixed precision training is crucial for maximizing throughput on modern GPU hardware. FSDP provides built-in support for mixed precision via the MixedPrecision policy."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"from torch.distributed.fsdp import MixedPrecision

mixed_precision_policy = MixedPrecision(
    param_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    reduce_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    buffer_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)

model = FSDP(
    model,
    auto_wrap_policy=my_auto_wrap_policy,
    mixed_precision=mixed_precision_policy,
    device_id=torch.cuda.current_device()
)"},{"order":16,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"FSDP is an essential tool in the modern PyTorch ecosystem for distributed training. By properly configuring auto-wrapping policies and mixed-precision settings, you can scale large language models and vision transformers efficiently across clusters."}]
